title: Self-hosting: run ork on its own repo safely

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Retrospective R1 (docs/review-2026-10-25-relay-retrospective.md). The owner wants ork developed through ork, so the ork repo runs relays on itself. A slice can change the engine or daemon that runs it. adj 166 (engine.self-host, open; recommended main-binary-restart).

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/daemon/handlers.go:88` and `internal/daemon/handlers.go:249`: the build id the daemon reports; compare it with the base branch head (proposed).
- `internal/cli/wave.go` and `internal/tui/waves.go`: refuse or warn on a wave with two slices whose Files touch `internal/engine`, `internal/daemon` or `cmd` (proposed).
- `internal/tui/view.go`: the restart offer once no run is active (proposed).
- `docs/design.md:8-60` (Shape) and `docs/state.md`: the self-host rules.
- S103 already clears a stale build marker after a daemon restart; reuse it.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- TestWavePlanWarnsOnTwoEngineSlices: two items whose Files list `internal/engine` paths give a plan warning (or refusal, per adj 166).
- TestRestartOfferedAfterEngineSliceCommits: a committed run whose diff touches `internal/daemon` sets a restart offer that shows only when no run is active.
- TestDaemonBuildBehindBaseBranch: a build id older than the base branch head is reported as behind.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Wait for adj 166. Re-anchor Files from the code first. The daemon keeps running the binary it started from; nothing runs from a worktree build. Use the build id (`daemon.build-id`, adj 102) to tell the owner the daemon is behind main. Mark any wording proposed until decided.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: go test -race ./internal/daemon ./internal/cli ./internal/tui; go vet; gofmt -l; slicer check; adj lint. UI slice: UI pass (r14).
